hypothesis: The magnitude of the real-time four-week initial claims ratio provides monotone incremental information about a two-month unemployment increase, beyond an intercept-only frequency.
model: sigmoid(logit(b)+beta*x); b=(past_target_events+1)/(past_target_cases+2); x=clip(log(ratio)/log(1.10),-3,3); beta>=0 minimizes SUM historical Bernoulli negative log likelihood + beta^2/2 with offset logit(b) fixed
training_clock: historical-origin frozen claims features and base UNRATE; labels initially available by current cut only
acceptance: at least5percent lower paired Brier than BOTH frequency baselines and strictly lower than persistence; exploratory screen only, never automatic prospective admission
missing_policy: exclude from all compared scores; no imputation, no nonconsecutive weeks, no revised-current-history substitution
retuning: none; single form/scale/clip/ridge/window fixed before calculation. Adaptive follow-up to binary AV153; that history/results already known, not confirmatory.
solver: Derivative monotone; beta=0 if derivative at zero>=0; otherwise double upper bound from1 until derivative>=0 and run100 bisections.
reporting: All eligible paired months including pandemic; annual breakdown descriptive; no selecting years, no rescues or parameter search.
